title: 3-Coloring by treewidth
task: Can the vertices of G be colored with at most three colors so that adjacent vertices have different colors?
encoding: A finite simple undirected graph G.
parameter: The intrinsic treewidth t of G.
coverage: Deterministic ETH and FPT ≠ W[1] bounds.

reader.parameter: The intrinsic treewidth t of G.

bounds.statement: Under ETH, no deterministic algorithm decides 3-Coloring within the stated running time.

reader.label: Subexponential bound in treewidth
reader.title: Subexponential bound in treewidth under ETH

sourceBasis.step: A treewidth-subexponential algorithm would also be subexponential in the number of vertices, since treewidth is at most the graph order.

bounds.statement: Under FPT ≠ W[1], no deterministic algorithm decides 3-Coloring within the stated running time.

reader.label: Effective subexponential bound in treewidth
reader.title: Effective subexponential bound in treewidth under FPT ≠ W[1]

sourceBasis.step: The logarithmic-pathwidth hardness gives a fixed-parameter reduction from Clique whose output pathwidth is at most a computable parameter factor times the logarithm of the graph order. Treewidth is at most that pathwidth. The effective cutoff would turn the claimed solver into a fixed-parameter algorithm for Clique.

recoveryAssessments.comparison: The bound reaches the historical treewidth exponent scale on the same inputs, with a computable cutoff for each prescribed saving.
